full_judgment:
2. Facts, in brief, are that the Election Commission, respondent No. I had declared the election schedule for holding the 10th Parliamentary Election for the Jatio Sangshad. The petitioner aspiring to contest the said election from the Constituency No. 280, Chittagong-3 (Sandip) along with others submitted respective nomination papers before the Returning Officer concern. However, on 5-12-2013 the date so fixed for scrutiny and selection of the nomination papers of the intending candidates for the said constituency the respondent No. 5, the Commerce Bank Ltd. submitted a report to the Returning Officer on the credit position of the petitioner stating, inter-alia, that he along with his other co-sharers had a loan liability with the said bank having inherited from his deceased father, who actually took the loan from the said bank and defaulted in repaying the same. In the said report the petitioner bank also pointed out that the bank obtained a decree of Taka 3,05,00,000 (Taka Three crores five lacs) only against the petitioner and other successive heirs of late Mr Mustafizur Rahman passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka in Money Suit No. 12 of 2002; that challenging the said decree First Appeal No. 80 of 2003 had been preferred, which is pending in the High Court Division. In this regard it has also been contended that meanwhile, all further proceedings of Money Execution Case No. 25 of 2004 so had been filed by the decree holder bank for execution of the decree passed in Money Suit No. 12 of 2002, had been stayed by the High Court Division vide order dated 7-5-2004 in Civil Rule No. 252(F)/2004 arising out of said First Appeal (Annexure-A). However, in the said report it has also been stated that the name of the petitioner was not enlisted in the CIB data base of the Bangladesh Bank, as defaulter. 

 8. Mr AF Hasan Ariff, the learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr Md Ashik-al Jalil, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that at the time of scrutiny of the nomination paper of the petitioner the respondent No. 5, the Commerce Bank Ltd. submitted a report to the Returning Officer concern on the credit position of the petitioner stating, inter alia, that he along with his other co-sharers had a loan liability with the bank concern having inherited from his deceased father, who actually took the loan from the said bank and defaulted in repaying the same within the prescribed period of time. In the said report the respondent bank had also pointed out that the Bank obtained a judgment and decree of Taka 3,05,00,000 (Taka Three crores five lacs) only against the petitioner and 10 (ten) other successive heirs of late Mr Mustafizur Rahman passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka in Money Suit No. 12 of 2002 and that challenging the said judgment and decree the respondent Bank had preferred appeal bearing First Appeal No. 80 of 2003, which is pending before this Hon'ble Court. However, in the said report, he submits that the respondent Bank had categorically mentioned that the name of the petitioner was not enlisted in the CI8 data base of Bangladesh Bank as defaulter. 

 10. Mr Shamsuddin Babul, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondent No. 6, another contesting candidate, submits that admittedly the petitioner was the principal defendant who had been impleaded as party in connection with Money Suit No. 12 of 2002 now pending before the learned Joint District Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 2, Dhaka and that the said suit had ultimately been decreed vide judgment and, decree dated 1-10-2002 where the petitioner had been directed to pay the decretal amount to the tune of Taka 3,05,00,000 with interest within the prescribed period of time. However, since the Adalat did not pass decree upon the claimed amount the Bank concern being aggrieved preferred First Appeal No. 80 of 2003 before the High Court Division, which is still pending for hearing and disposal. In that view of the matter he submits that the petitioner being a defaulter is a disqualified candidate in view of Article 12(1) clause (1) and (m) of the RPO of 1972. 

 11. He further goes to submit that in the affidavit হলফনামা the petitioner did not mention about the pendency of the said First Appeal which had been preferred pursuant to the judgment and decree passed by the concerned Artha Rin Adalat and hence, on that count the prayer of the petitioner should be knocked down for suppression of fact. 

 13. Admittedly, the father of the petitioner having defaulted to pay the loan amount within the prescribed period of time Commercial Bank Ltd. instituted Money Suit No. 12 of 2002 before the concerned court of law impleading the petitioner being his son and 10 others being the successive heirs, as defendants. Ultimately, the said suit had been decreed vide judgment and decree dated 1-10-2002 giving direction upon the petitioner and others, the judgment debtors to pay up the decretal amount within a prescribed period of time. Having defaulted the decree holder bank filed Artha Execution Case No. 25 of 2004 before the executing Adalat. However, challenging the judgment and decree so passed in Money Suit No. 12 of 2002 the decree holder Bank had preferred First Appeal No.80 of 2003 before this Court. Meanwhile, vide order dated 17-5-2004 this Court had stayed all further proceedings of the said execution case in connection with Civil Rule No. 252(F)/2004 arising out of said First Appeal. 

 14. In the given context, the issue which requires determination in the present Rule Nisi is when evidently the father of the petitioner took loan from the bank concern and having defaulted to pay the said amount and also having died meanwhile the petitioner and others being the successive heirs of the loanee having been impleaded in Money Suit No.12 of 2002 as defendants and ultimately, the judgment and decree having been passed against them as judgment debtors whether the petitioner being one of the judgment debtors who aspires to contest 10th Parliamentary Election for Constituency No. 280, Chittagong-3 (sandip) is disqualified to contest the said election within the meaning of Article 12(1)(1) and (m) of the Representation of People Order, 1972. 

 27. The claim of the respondent No.6 to identify the petitioner as "loan defaulter" is rooted in the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat concern in Money Suit No. 12 of 2002 against him and others as judgment debtors. Evidently, said Money Suit had been instituted by the respondent-bank impleading the petitioner and others being the successive heirs of their predecessor late Mr Mustafizur Rahman who took loan from the said bank but ultimately, failed to pay up the said amount within the prescribed period of time. 

 29. The respondent No.6 has miserably failed to show that the petitioner himself has taken loan in his personal capacity or has taken loan as a Director of a company or firm and that he or the said company or firm has defaulted to pay the defaulted loan amount within the stipulated period of time. Moreover, no where within the four corners of the RPO of 1972 i t has disqualified an aspirant candidate for the judgment and decree being passed by the concerned court of law against him in the capacity of a successive heir for the loan default of his predecessor (in the present case, his father). 

 31. The further contention of the respon-dent No.6 is the non-disclosure in the "হলফনামা", affidavit of the judgment and decree being passed against the petitioner in Money Suit No.12 of 2002 by the Artha Rin Adalat concern. Article 12(1) Explanation VII clause (3b)(f) in this regard provides as under— 

 33. Against the said respective column the candidate is required to give information of taking loan either by himself or jointly or by any member who is dependent on him or in the capacity of a Chairman, Managing Director or Director of any bank or financial institution. The respondent No.6 does not come forward with any document whatsoever to show that the petitioner either has taken loan in his personal capacity or by any member who is dependent on him or in the capacity of a Chairman, Managing Director or Director of any bank or financial institution. Moreover, there is no column in the হলফনামা as to whether any judgment and decree has been passed by any court of law in connection with loan default. As such, the contention of the respondent No. 6 to that effect, falls through. Moreover, said plea has not been raised by the respondent No. 6 at the time of hearing of the appeal before the Election Commission nor on the said ground nomination of the petitioner has been cancelled. 

 36. In the report dated 1-12-2013, as produced by the bank concern, the respondent No. 5 before the Returning Officer concern (as quoted above) it has been stated, inter alia, বর্তমানে সিআইবি ডাটা বেইজে জনাব ABM Mahfuzur Rahman Mita মনোনীত প্রার্থী চট্টগ্রাম-৩ আসনে সংরক্ষিত নেই।” In other words, the name of the petitioner is not included in the CIB report. Moreover, in the said report it has been clearly stated by the said Bank that loan has been taken by the father of the petitioner and having defaulted to pay within time Money Suit No.12 of 2002 has been instituted against the petitioner and 10 others being the successive heirs. In the absence of any information in the CIB data base with regard to the petitioner and disregarding the report of respondent bank dated 1-12-2013 finding the petitioner as "defaulter" under Article 12(1) of the RPO of 1972 by the Election Commission on the basis of the contention of respondent No. 6, who has based his standing on the judgment and decree passed in Money Suit No.12 of 2002, and thereby declaring him as disqualified from contesting the 10th Parliamentary Election, is an order passed without jurisdiction.
